en.question: You are wrapping the Claude API behind an internal service used by several product teams. Which two practices most improve operability? (Select 2)

options.text: Emit structured logs with model, token counts, stop_reason, and latency per call.
Expose model and parameters as configuration rather than per-caller literals.
Cache every response permanently so repeated questions never reach the API.
options.note: Unbounded permanent caching serves stale answers and grows without limit.

options.text: Let each team supply its own API key so usage is attributed to that team.
options.note: Key sprawl multiplies rotation and revocation work; attribute usage with metadata.

options.text: Strip stop_reason from responses so callers need not handle it.
options.note: Hiding stop_reason removes the field callers most need to detect truncation.

en.explanation: Those logs are what make cost, truncation, and latency debuggable across all consumers, and centralised configuration lets you change model or parameters without touching callers.
